title: Prepare a forearm crutch for reuse
instruction: Prepare this crutch for its owner.
context: A worn-through rubber ferrule exposes the aluminum tube, which can slip under a person. The starting fault must be recognized from the object. This task assesses fitting and visible retention of the foot; it does not certify patient weight-bearing strength.
setup: On a bench at z=74.75 cm: a full-size 90 cm aluminum forearm crutch with polymer cuff and handgrip, 22 mm shaft diameter, 388.579 g without its foot. Native origin (15,-24,79.2) cm; native +Z axis points along world (0.4,0.916515,0), native +X upward. It settles onto its side. A 42 g worn rubber ferrule (a matching ferrule cut down; grip 4.8 N normal, about 3.0 N to pull off) is initially fitted: original envelope 38 mm maximum diameter and 45 mm height, bottom 12 mm missing; the metal tube projects 4 mm beyond the cut face. A matching 50 g replacement ferrule, 38 mm lower/30 mm upper outside diameter and 45 mm high, 8 mm sole, stands separately on its sole at (35,-5,74.77) cm, bore vertical and mouth upward. Its compliant free bore is 21.6 mm across, fitting the 22 mm shaft. Loose distractors: a blue plastic marker, 10.9x0.8x0.7 cm, 8 g, at (60,-50,74.75) cm; and a metal/plastic slotted screwdriver, 14.8x2.7x2.6 cm, 36.47 g, at (65,-35,74.75) cm. Positions refer to asset origins. Exact geometry and rotations are included; there is no clamp or concealed support.
scoring: Score 0 otherwise. Score 0.5 requires: the worn foot's sampled bore axis is more than 35 mm from the shaft centerline, inside the specified bench area, below 30 mm/s translation and 0.3 rad/s rotation, with fingertips more than 65 mm away; the replacement is seated within 1 mm radial offset, 2 mm axial offset of the sole stop, and 3 degrees axis error, with fingertips more than 65 mm from its origin; and unsupported retention has been observed. Retention requires the shaft pointing upward at least 60 degrees, the foot at least 25 mm above the bench, fingertips more than 65 mm from the foot origin, and no external foot support for 30 elapsed 20 Hz intervals (1.5 seconds). Both crutch and foot must remain within 3 mm translation and 3 degrees rotation of their initial window poses. Retention proof is cleared if radial separation exceeds 3 mm, axial offset leaves [-5,4] mm, or axis error exceeds 7 degrees; a new valid retention check can restore it. Removal alone earns nothing. For 0.5, all task-object origins and measured crutch extremities must remain above bench height minus 30 mm. Score 1.0 additionally requires the repaired assembly released on its side for 20 elapsed intervals (1 second), using the same 3 mm/3 degree pose window: the foot and cuff lowest points within 3 mm of bench height, absolute vertical shaft-axis component below 0.20, measured extremities inside x=(-17,89) cm and y=(-63,63) cm, fingertips more than 50 mm from the shaft and 30 mm from handgrip/cuff, and no direct robot contact with the crutch or replacement foot and no contact path to a robot through the movable worn foot, marker or screwdriver. Fixed bench and room supports do not connect such paths. The worn-foot bench bounds are x=(-15,87) cm and y=(-61,61) cm; its lower sampled axial endpoint must lie from 20 mm below to 45 mm above bench height. Read-only contact observations sample all bodies at 480 Hz, with a 0.0001 N numerical-zero tolerance. Invalid/nonfinite poses score zero. A recoverable drop does not permanently prevent later success.
reset_notes: Simulation: restore the fixed source poses, worn foot fitted and replacement separate; scorer history resets only through the simulator reset. Real trials (README has the full steps): make the worn foot by cutting a new matching ferrule square 12.0 mm up from its tread (33.0 +-0.5 mm left, sole gone); push it on until its mouth meets a line 37.0 mm from the tube end, so the tube projects 4.0 +-0.5 mm (caliper depth rod). Its axial pull-off, by a cord loop on the collar shoulder and a peak-hold luggage scale at about 1 cm/s, must read 2.5-3.5 N in three pulls (model: 3.0 N); recheck each session and every 10 trials, retire when out of range, torn or after 50 trials. Replacement: pull-off at least 20 N (model 30 N), retired after 20 fittings. Wipe tube and bores dry at each reset. No patient is present.
fidelity: Full-size crutch and native robot. Rigid shaft; rubber uses 12 radial sectors, 20 kN/m and 3 Ns/m each, with friction fit and no attachment. Bore/bevel planes are preserved with small outer-bevel clipping. No local axial strain, tearing or patient-load model; properties are estimates. Rigid-contact solver produces brief force spikes; shaft deformation is not modeled. Native cameras unchanged; wrist inspection reveals initial wear. Supplemental foot view.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 after 1,680 control steps; scripted demo: 1.0 in each of two complete trials (1,627 steps each).
